verses.1: And he got up and went away. Then Johanan arrived in the city.
verses.2: And David came to Ahimelech, the priest. Ahimelech was afraid when he saw David. He said to him, “Who are you, and where is your companion?”
verses.3: And David said to Ahimelech, the king’s priest: “I command you to tell me one thing.” He replied, “I will not reveal what I am ordered to say. I know where the young men are, but I cannot tell you where they are.”
verses.4: And now, what do you have under your hand? Give me five loaves of bread.
verses.5: And the priest said to David, “There is no bread under my hand. If there is any bread that is holy, then it must be kept for the priests alone.”
verses.6: And David angered the priest, and said to him, “If a woman is given to us as a wife, then she should be treated with respect. She should be like all other young women; she should be considered sacred. Even though today she is considered sacred among us.”
verses.7: And the priest gave him sacred bread, because there was no bread available there. It seems that the bread that was forbidden from being used before Jehovah should be used on that day instead.
verses.8: And there was a man among Shaul’s servants on that day. He was arrested before Jehovah. His name was Dohayim, the captain of the evil ones who served Shaul.
verses.9: And David said to Ahimelech, “There is not a single arrow or spear under your control. For I have not taken any of those things into my hands, because it was the king’s property.”
verses.10: And the priest said, “This is the tunic of the Philistine woman you took captive at the Valley of Ain. Now, she is with you in your tent. If you want to take her with you, then do so. There’s no other tunic like this.” And David said, “There’s no such gift that I can give you.”
verses.11: And David rose up and fled that day from Saul. He went to Achish, the king of Gath.
verses.12: And the servants of Ahasuerus said to him, “No, this is David, king of the earth. Do not answer them with insults. Say instead, ‘Shaul struck his thousands, and David his ten thousand.’”
verses.13: And David put these words in his heart. He saw great things from the face of Achish, king of Gath.
verses.14: And they changed their manner of speaking in their own eyes. They cursed with their hands, and they stood at the doors of the gates. Then they rushed back to their elders.
verses.15: And Achiš said to his servants, “Look! There’s a man who is suffering. What will you bring him before me?”
verses.16: I have no need for anything else, since you’ve brought this over to torment me. This will bring me to my house.
